#3289. How to Set Up Alexa Wishlist Alerts for Black Friday and Cyber Monday

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale."

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

#3288. Anthony Clark’s Official Cause Of Death Revealed

An official cause of death for Yes, Dear star Anthony Clark has been reported: The comedian, who passed November 10 at 63, died from septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism also included as underlying conditions. Acute kidney failure is added as a significant contributing factor.

The details comes from a death certificate obtained by People magazine late yesterday.

The death of Clark, who started his career as a stand-up comedian and later became the star of TV sitcoms Boston Common and Yes, Dear, was announced earlier this month via a social media post from his Yes, Dear co-star and friend Mike O’Malley. Deadline reported at the time that initial reports indicated his death was connected to complications related to pneumonia and the flu. (Clark’s age has been variously reported as 62 and 63). Related Stories News 'Scream' Actor C.W. Morgan's Cause Of Death Revealed Obituaries Anthony Clark Dies: Comedian And 'Yes, Dear' Star Was 62

Clark was best known for starring alongside Mike O’Malley, Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder on the 2000 CBS sitcom Yes, Dear. Created and executive produced by Greg Garcia and Alan Kirschenbaum, the comedy about two couples living under the same roof ran for six seasons. Watch on Deadline

On hearing the news of Clark’s death, Garcia, who also created NBC’s My Name I Earl, shared the following thoughts with Deadline:

I’ve been very lucky to be friends with some of the funniest people in the world, and Anthony Clark had the most insane sense of humor of all of them. The things that would come out of his mouth were so unexpected and hilarious. Over the last two or three years we had reconnected, and I always looked forward to our monthly phone calls where we would catch up and make each other laugh. Recently, he was so full of joy and encouragement when he found out I was trying stand-up comedy for the first time. He enjoyed talking about the art of stand-up, being on the road, and would also offer some great advice. Just a few weeks ago we were laughing hysterically on the phone, trading jokes and telling stories. It’s a sad day, and I’ll miss him very much. I’m glad he was able to bring a lot of joy and laughter into the world.

#3287. iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a convenient new setting, here’s how to use it

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of new features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

But Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a new setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

While wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

New in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

You can also move the new slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

According to a new report from Bloomberg, Apple’s head of camera and photo software retired last month. Jon McCormack spent eight years at Apple and “oversaw the Camera and Photos apps and the underlying technology that determines how users capture, view, and edit their pictures and video.”

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Mark Gurman reports that Apple hasn’t named a new vice president to replace McCormack, who reported to software chief Craig Federighi. “Instead, his former deputies are assuming his responsibilities under other executives,” the report says.

In his role, McCormack oversaw “close coordination between software engineers and Apple’s camera hardware and chip teams.” He’s credited with last year’s redesigned selfie camera and other projects:

His work included the redesigned selfie camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup last year. This year, Apple added a variable-aperture camera to the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, giving users more control over lighting and depth of field. The company also introduced a customizable Camera app interface with professional controls.

Bloomberg describes McCormack as a “strong opponent of using generative AI to create or alter photographs,” a philosophy that created tension as Apple embraced AI tools in the Photos app. His retirement, however, “wasn’t related to a disagreement or clash with Apple over its AI strategy,” the report says.

McCormack spoke in depth about iOS 27 features like Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing in an interview with Tyler Stalman in June. He emphasized how the features “preserve the integrity of the moment.”

#3283. Lincoln Center Theater Names Naomi Weinstock New Executive Director Of Development; Robert Jones Upped

New York’s Lincoln Center Theater has appointed Naomi Weinstock as Executive Director of Development, a position in which she will set the direction for LCT’s contributed revenue and lead the development team in building the resources for realize the organization’s artistic and institutional ambitions.

As the Executive Director, Weinstock will serve as a strategic partner to LCT’s artistic leadership and Board of Directors, tasked with championing “the theater’s artistic vision and driving philanthropic investment across all of its stages.” Related Stories Reviews 'A Few Good Men' Broadway Review: Bradley Whitford And Tom Blyth Manhandle The Truth News Krysta Rodriguez Joins 'A Few Good Men' Broadway Revival Starring Bradley Whitford And Tom Blyth; Complete Cast & Creative Team Announced

Weinstock joins LCT from New York City Center, where she has served as Vice President and Chief Development Officer since 2018. Watch on Deadline

In a related move, LCT promoted Robert Jones to Chief Brand and Strategy Officer, effective immediately. Both he and Weinstock will report to Managing Director Mike Schleifer and serve on LCT’s executive team, alongside Kewsong Lee Artistic Director Lear deBessonet, Schleifer, Executive Producer Bartlett Sher, Stacey and Eric Mindich Producer Nicole Kastrinos, and Helen Gurley Brown Artistic Director of LCT3 and Producer Maria Manuela Goyanes.

“We are thrilled to welcome Naomi to Lincoln Center Theater, and back to the Lincoln Center campus,” said Lear deBessonet and Mike Schleifer in a statement. “She brings an extraordinary depth of experience, a demonstrated ability to build and maintain meaningful relationships with supporters, and a track record of securing the kind of transformational philanthropic investment that allows an institution to think ambitiously about its future. She has a reputation as a thoughtful, respected leader, and we’re very lucky to have her join the team.”

“I am honored to be joining Lear, Mike, and the executive team at Lincoln Center Theater, an organization I have long admired. There is an energy at the theater right now that is impossible to miss. I look forward to working with the Board, staff, and community of supporters to build upon an extraordinary legacy and help shape LCT’s next great chapter,” said Weinstock.

Jones, who joined LCT in the summer of 2025 as Chief Marketing Officer, assumes an expanded role as Chief Brand and Strategy Officer. In this position, he will lead overall identity, positioning, and reputation of the institution, with responsibility for the integrated strategy and execution of LCT’s marketing, advertising, publicity, communications, partnerships, sales, customer experience, and merchandising. His expanded remit reflects the theater’s commitment to building a distinctive institutional brand and deepening its relationship with audiences, while aligning the organization’s mission and artistic vision with its business objectives and public identity.

“We are thrilled to recognize Robert Jones with this expanded role at Lincoln Center Theater,” said deBessonet and Schleifer. “Our vision for the organization extends far beyond individual shows, centering how we serve our mission in the culture at large. Robert has distinguished himself as a remarkable leader in how we define ourselves as an institution, build relationships with our audiences, and shape our place in the cultural landscape. We look forward to this expanded role for an integral member of our team.”

#3281. The Best Amazon Prime Benefits You Probably Don't Know About

If you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

If you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the company is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

The standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Amazon Health: Prime users get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

#3280. SkyShowtime Staff Complained About Workplace Culture & Handling Of “Racist Conduct” Before Comcast/Skydance Shuttered Streamer

EXCLUSIVE: Comcast and Skydance announced this week that they planned to shutter SkyShowtime for commercial reasons, but behind the scenes, the U.S. media giants have also been addressing serious unrest among employees at the joint-venture streamer.

Deadline can reveal that a group of SkyShowtime staff lodged a formal complaint in June about the company’s workplace culture, citing concerns including favoritism, retaliation against staff raising grievances, and the handling of alleged “racist conduct” by an unnamed manager.

SkyShowtime’s board, which is comprised of representatives from Comcast and Skydance, engaged external law firm Osborne Clarke to investigate. The board shared the outcome of the review with aggrieved employees this week, informing them that “appropriate action has been taken.” The response landed on the same day staff were told that SkyShowtime would be closed. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News CBS News Staffers Take Buyout Offers As Skydance Looks For Cost Savings News Biggest ITV Shows Like 'Love Island' & 'I'm A Celebrity' To Remain Free-To-Air Once Sky Deal Completes

Deadline understands that SkyShowtime employee unrest had been percolating for months before the group complaint, with Deadline reporting in May that mood metrics had been below benchmarks. Some staffers also had misgivings about the amount of time CEO Monty Sarhan was spending in Philadelphia when he was running a business headquartered in London. At the time, senior SkyShowtime figures denied that morale was low and insisted that Sarhan was based in the UK.

In their June complaint, around 25 anonymous employees raised at least five key concerns and questioned the leadership of Sarhan and Richard Thurston, SkyShowtime’s chief HR officer. Deadline has seen an email the employees sent SkyShowtime’s board earlier this month summarizing their position.

“We have chosen to remain anonymous because of the nature of these concerns and because a previous employee who raised similar issues through internal channels was subsequently dismissed. Employees should not have to risk adverse consequences to raise legitimate concerns,” the employees said in their November 2 email.

They listed their concerns as follows: “Inadequate responses to complaints of racist conduct by a manager; favouritism and unequal treatment of employees; promotion, levelling and compensation disparities influenced by personal proximity; selective resourcing and inconsistent treatment across functions; and retaliation against employees who have raised concerns.”

They specifically questioned if Thurston was the right person to wind down SkyShowtime, arguing that employees must have confidence that decisions will be “handled fairly, consistently and transparently” at a time of “significant uncertainty about their livelihoods.”

“We recognise the difficult circumstances facing the company. But a difficult transition is precisely when accountability matters most. We urge you to ensure that appropriate action follows and that employees can have confidence in the fairness of the process,” they continued.

The SkyShowtime board responded to the employees this week. A board representative said: “As you are aware, your concerns were reviewed by an external law firm. The investigation has now been completed, the findings have been carefully considered, and appropriate action has been taken.

Sarhan and Thurston are among the executives leaving SkyShowtime ahead of the business shuttering by late 2027. They have both stepped back from day-to-day operations and are on gardening leave.

SkyShowtime’s position is that their departure is for commercial reasons and is unrelated to the external investigation. In an internal email this week, the SkyShowtime board thanked Sarhan for his “commitment and contributions.” Deadline offered Sarhan and Thurston the opportunity to comment through reps from Comcast and Skydance.

Mark Neil, SkyShowtime’s CFO, will become interim general manager as the company winds down. Based out of Sky’s campus on the outskirts of central London, SkyShowtime employs around 300 people. Most of them will face an uncertain future, with employees in consultation about their jobs.

Deadline first revealed concerns about the venture in May, when we reported that Skydance’s proposed ownership of HBO Max would put the David Ellison-run company in breach of its joint venture agreement with Comcast. Last year, Deadline revealed that the shareholders had ploughed $1 billion into SkyShowtime, even though it remained loss-making.

Commenting on the external investigation, a SkyShowtime spokesperson said: “Concerns that were raised were reviewed by an external law firm. The review is complete and the findings have been carefully considered, and appropriate action has been taken.”

Google is upgrading the Gemini app on Mac with computer use capabilities that can work across local desktop applications and the web.

Which popular wearable will come out on top?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I walked 5,018 steps over roughly 45 minutes with the Apple Watch Series 12 on my left wrist and the Garmin Venu 4 on my right. This is the second time I’ve pitted these two similarly priced and capable wearables — two of the best smartwatches in 2026 — against one another in a test of fitness tracking accuracy supremacy.

Last time these two met, Garmin eked out a win over its Apple rival, but not by a huge margin. For this test, as in the past, the primary metric we’ll use to compare overall performance is total step count.

While step count isn’t necessarily the most important workout data point, it is one I can easily manually count (with some help from my trusty, clicky tally counter) and use as a primary control. For other metrics, including pace, distance, and climb, I logged the walk using Strava on my iPhone 16 Plus.

Find the results of my Apple Watch 12 vs. Garmin Venu 4 walk test: Round 2 below, along with five takeaways from the data and the overall winner.

The Garmin Venu 4 is one of the brand's most stylish and well-rounded smartwatches, balancing impressive workout features with useful smart features. It's also on sale for a sizable discount ahead of the 2026 holidays.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is the brand's latest flagship model, released only a few months ago. Despite that, it just dropped to its lowest-ever price for Black Friday 2026.

During my 45-minute walk around hilly, leafy Seattle, Washington, I counted exactly 5,018 steps, a tally Stava matched precisely.

When it comes to judging overall accuracy for a walk of this length, I consider any step count tally that's within 100 steps of my actual count to be excellent. This is to say, both the Apple Watch 12 and Garmin Venu 4 did exceptionally well here.

But Apple was a little bit closer, with a total that's only 12 steps off from my actual one compared to 22 steps for the Garmin. On the flip side, Garmin's distance tally is a tad closer to the control (Strava), but again, both watches were within a reasonable margin for error.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Even the best Apple Watch models sometimes inflate climb data, at least in my experience, and that appears to be the case here. Still, I'd rather have my Apple Watch consistently overcount by around 20 feet during my walks than undercount by that amount.

Garmin came a lot closer to matching Strava's climb data — a predictable outcome — with a total that's off by only seven feet.

Current Apple Watches don't record an average moving pace, unlike Garmin and Strava, only an elapsed or total average pace for your walks/runs/bike rides/etc. For this walk, Apple's average is a little slower than Strava's, while Garmin's is considerably slower.

That said, when comparing Strava and Garmin's moving pace metric, the two align much more closely. Strava logged 17 ins 22 secs per mile compared to 17 mins 29 secs for Garmin.

Garmin's average and maximum heart rate recordings are noticeably higher than Apple's, which is a bit perplexing. Ultimately, this was a fairly leisurely walk, with only a few blocks of steep hills. Which is to say, Apple's heart rate data looks right on the money to me, while Garmin's suggests a higher intensity than I expected.

Despite that, the Venu 4 noted fewer overall calories burned during my ~45-minute walk than Apple.

Ladies and gentlemen, we have a new champion! With a more accurate step-count total and average elapsed pace data, the Apple Watch Series 12 beats the Garmin Venu 4 in this second round of fitness-tracking performance supremacy.

This, of course, means that a round three is in order. Stay tuned for that! In the meantime, which of these two watches do you prefer? Let me know in the poll below.

#3277. These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this new feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a new setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the big screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.)

That’s similar walk-up business to Wicked two years (37%), and higher than last year’s Wicked: For Good (26%), but it’s lower than Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (47%). Realize though that movie didn’t have a majority of fans buying tickets in advance like Sunrise on the Reaping (54% to 64%).

Women at 68% remain the big turnout for the latest Hunger Games movie which is no surprise. Forty-nine percent of the women who saw the movie came with one friend or more to watch the film (similar to Songbirds & Snakes 50% who came with one to five people), while 22% came with a date, spouse or partner (same as the 2023 film). The overall audience at 64% bought tickets because it’s for a franchise they love, while 33% said it was because of the cast.

Diversity demos on Sunrise on the Reaping are 49% Caucasian, 27% Latino and Hispanic, 9% Black and 9% Asian American, which is similar to the previous pic’s 50% Caucasian, 24% Latino and Hispanic and 10% apiece for Black and Asian American audiences. The percentage of 18-34 year olds showing up remained huge at 74% for Sunrise versus 76% for Songbirds & Snakes.

Sunrise on the Reaping currently is the fourth best opening in the franchise, but will likely be the third best, overtaking 2014’s Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1 ($55.1M Friday/previews and $121.8M 3-day) by tomorrow. The top two domestic starts in the Collins series are 2013’s Catching Fire ($70.9M Friday/previews, $158M 3-day) and the original 2012 Hunger Games ($67.2M Friday/previews and $152.5M opening). Catching Fire stills stands as Lionsgate’s top opening at the domestic B.O.

Amazon MGM Studio’s I Play Rocky is coming in ligher than expected with $9.3M despite scoring a rare A+ CinemaScore (which no Rocky movie in CinemaScore history has done even though this pic is about the making of the 1976 Sylvester Stallone movie). Note the movie is older skewing with 52% over 45, and that audience will take their time to come out, likely discovering the movie later this week. The exits here are powerful enough with an 87% definite recommend. 59% to 41% male-to-female with 50% men over 25, 37% women over 25 and 9% men under 25 and 5% women under 25. Very strong positive scores and definite recommends in every single demo. Caucasian turnout at 57%, Latino and Hispanic at 22%, Black at 8% (giving pic a 100%), Asian American at 7%, and Native American at 7% (also a 100% score).

No major PLFs on this pic. The Peter Farrelly directed movie is playing best in the West, East and South Central. To give you an idea of how older skewing it is, the Cinemark Palace 21 in Boca Raton, FL is the leading single-location gross at $11.2K yesterday.

The entire theatrical marketplace is around $172.1M, just -5% off from a year ago when Wicked: For Good opened to a franchise best of $147M. With no Moana, Zootopia, or Wicked in the marketplace, there was some concern that we would hit a dry spell at the Thanksgiving box office, which would be unfortunate given the great resurgence we’ve had at the domestic box office, now coursing to $9B by the end the holiday with an eye at $10B by the end of the year. Thanks to Lionsgate, Sunrise on the Reaping is going to get us through. With Disney’s Hexed and Universal’s Focker-in-Law expected to post around $45M a piece over the Wednesday-Sunday stretch, it wouldn’t be shocking if Hunger Games takes the lead with $50M+ over the 5-day box office as the franchise typically rallies over the Thanksgiving holiday.

Focus Features’ highly buzzed Andrew Scott Best Actor movie Elsinore is seeing a solid opening theater average of $40K from 6 theaters in NYC and LA for a 3-day of $240K. Friday was $140K with $33K coming from AMC Lincoln Square and LA’s AMC Grove with $32K. Both had Q&As boosting ticket sales. RT critics are at 87% certified fresh.

Sumerian’s acquisition of the Sundance Grand Jury Prize and Audience winning drama Josephine from Beth de Araújo is looking at an estimated $35K Friday and 3-day of $138K at four locations in NY and LA. AMC Burbank is leading the way with $15K yesterday. The Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan starring pic is 97% certified fresh with RT critics. Opening per theater for the weekend is $34,5K.

Mubi has the Andrey Zvyagintsev directed crime thriller Minotaur which is France’s international film Oscar entry. The pic did $52K yesterday for what looks to be an estimated $123K opening at six sites in NY, LA, Toronto, San Francisco and Chicago. LA and NY are driving the ship with the latter’s Angelika Film Center minting $21K on Friday. The pic won Cannes’ Grand Prize of the Festival. Pic is 96% certified fresh with critics.

FRIDAY MIDDAY: Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is heading for the fourth highest opening for the Suzanne Collins franchise as of now with $110M stateside at 4,108 theaters after a Friday that’s $51M which includes those $21M previews. If the movie isn’t front-loaded, it has a shot at possibly becoming the third highest North American opening for the franchise.

The industry overseas outlook is $97M, which if that holds means a $206.7M global opening. That latter number is not according to Lionsgate. A high $80M+ foreign start is within reach.

Top Hunger Games openings at the North American B.O. belong to 2013’s Catching Fire ($70.9M Friday/previews, $158M 3-day); the original 2012 Hunger Games ($67.2M Friday/previews and $152.5M opening), and 2014’s Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1 ($55.1M Friday/previews and $121.8M 3-day). Sunrise on the Reaping is the sixth movie in the Collins’ franchise, the fifth directed by Francis Lawrence. Altogether the previous five movies count $3.3 billion at the worldwide box office.

Again, the jaw drop here is how this franchise turned its fortunes upward after hitting an all-time low in its opening three years ago with Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6M). Comps to other sixthquels are hard, and the opening jump between Songbirds & Sunrise is +147% — which is unheard of. The surge in domestic openings between Christopher Nolan’s Batman Begins and Dark Knight was +225%.

Among all openings in November at the domestic B.O., Sunrise on the Reaping is currently 13th in a list of 16 movies that have bowed to over $100M for the month.

RelishMix beams that the great word-of-mouth that the pic has “book loyalists showing up in full force, insisting this adaptation finally respects the source material. There’s trust running through the comments, ‘Director Francis Lawrence’s track record and the franchise’s unbroken prequel streak as reasons to believe this one sticks the landing,’ and, ‘We’ll need therapy after this,’ read as proof of the story’s emotional weight. Comments marvel, ‘Dang from Voldemort, Moriarty, Hades, and Ramses to President Snow, Ralph Fiennes catching literary villain roles like Pokémon.’ Others draw sharper comparison, saying ‘this is like the and/or of the Hunger Games I feel it, I know it, I read the book and they are going to break your heart.'”

Overall social media reach is 652M across TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, X and Facebook which is not far from The Odyssey‘s pre-opening reach at 680M and +66% above where Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes was in its social media universe, bowing shortly after the actors strike ended (393M). That 652M reach for Sunrise on the Reaping is 95% above other action-sci-fi-fantasy sub-genre features.

“Hunger Games cast activation index clocks 21 of 24 cast/creators activated with 40.4M total fans,” adds RelishMix in their weekly report.

“Notably, Jennifer Lawrence and her newly rebooted Instagram with 9.2M fans activated a video from Fallon shot in an elevator at 30 Rock with 25+M views and 40+M views on the Fallon IG. Activations also include McKenna Grace at 13M, Maya Hawke at 10.4M, Elle Fanning at 7.7M, Josh Hutcherson at 4.2M, Glenn Close at 1.3M, Joseph Zada at 442K and Whitney Peak at 492K. As well, some cast-off-the grid, include Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Woody Harrelson and Kieran Culkin.”

Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky from Amazon MGM Studios is looking at $10M in second place after a $3.9M Friday in its third frame 2,477 wide break and a running cume of $11M by EOD Sunday. The exits are excellent, so let’s hope there’s long legs on this Sylvester Stallone biopic which is 89% with Rotten Tomatoes critics and 98% with moviegoers.

No. 3 goes to the second weekend of Paramount’s Johnny Depp Ebenezer at 3,545 theaters with $2.1M today, a 3-day of $8M, -58%, and ten-day total by Sunday of $32.8M.

Fourth is Warner Bros’ The Cat in the Hat at 3,262 theaters, a third Friday of $1.7M, 3-day of $7.3M, -35%, and running cume of $47.5M.

Fifth is the third weekend of Gkids/Toho’s Godzilla Minus Zero with $2.9M, -66%, after a third Friday of $700K at 3,000 theaters. Running total by Sunday is $54.7M.

FRIDAY AM AFTER THURSDAY EXCLUSIVE: Lionsgate’s Francis Lawrence directed The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping came in with $21M in overall previews since Wednesday. As we told you, that’s the second best for the Suzanne Collins franchise behind Catching Fire‘s $25.2M in 2013 and the second best for 2026 behind Spider-Man: Brand New Day‘s $72M.

Note that all the movies that have posted $20M+ in previews went on to cross $100M+ in their opening weekends. This is a big deal for Lionsgate following its success with Michael, which went on to make $1 billion at the global box office, one of five movies to clear that threshold this year.

Out of the gate Thursday night, Screen Engine and Rentrak’s PostTrak shows 79% “definite recommend” and 5 stars with a 92% positive for general audiences. Women showed up at 67%, with 38% females under 25 and 29% over 25. Biggest definite recommends are from women under 25 (89%), the 13-17 set (92%) and 18-24 demo (82%). The 18-34 showed up at a massive 77%. Close to 70% of Thursday night’s audience bought their tickets within the past week or more than a week ago.

Excitement among fans was apparent a year ago this week, when Lionsgate dropped the first trailer for Sunrise on the Reaping: It went on to clock 109M views in its first 24 hours, becoming the second-most viewed trailer for Lionsgate after Michael‘s 116M global view traffic.

EXCLUSIVE: No Wicked, no Moana, no problem, because Lionsgate is saving the Thanksgiving week box office with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which is posting $21.25M in previews, the second-best ever for the franchise behind 2013’s Hunger Games: Catching Fire, which lit $25.2M in its previews. Sunrise‘s money is currently the second-best previews YTD after Sony’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($72M, $360M) and ahead of Universal’s The Odyssey ($17.6M previews, $123.5M opening).

RELATED: All The Best Picture Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Other previews that Sunrise on the Reaping is beating include Universal’s Wicked from two years ($19.2M; $112.5M opening); for the longest time we heard that the latest feature take of a Suzanne Collins novel was outstripping the presales of that female-skewing musical starring Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo. It’s also ahead of Lionsgate’s Michael ($12.6M previews, $97.2M opening), The Devil Wears Prada 2 ($10M, $76.7M opening) and light years ahead of the previous Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes ($5.75M previews, $44.6M opening), which had its campaign impacted by the 2023 actors strike, not to mention the Collins novel about the origins of Coriolanus Snow wasn’t a fan fave. Sunrise on the Reaping was beloved by fans in its early story about the Woody Harrelson mentor character, Haymitch Abernathy.

When it comes to the all-time preview record for a Lionsgate title, that belongs to The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2, which made $30.4M from midnight shows leading to a $141M opening back in mid-November 2012.

RELATED: All The Best Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Now, Sunrise on the Reaping‘s advance money was minted with $5M via early access PLF showtimes on Wednesday, with another $16.25M collected tonight per sources. Catching Fire‘s back in the day began warming up with 10 p.m. Thursday night shows. Note that Wicked‘s previews were composed of Amazon promotional screenings, Wednesday night PLF shows and an $8M Thursday.

With a great preview start, it’s fair to say that a $100M opening is well in store for the net-$150M priced Sunrise on the Reaping, especially with a 95% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, which is the best ever in the franchise ahead of Catching Fire (89%), Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (89%), Hunger Games (81%), Mockingjay Part 2 (71%), and Mockingjay Part 1 (66%).

Overseas, industry projects have risen from a $70M forecast to $86M opening.

RELATED: All The Best Actor Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Critics aren’t hot on the fifth Hunger Games movie from director Francis Lawrence (the original 2012 movie was helmed by Gary Ross) with an RT score of 68% fresh. However, even if Katniss was shooting Cupid’s arrows at critics, they’d still play hard to get, for the best reviews in the series were a a while ago with Catching Fire (90% certified fresh) and Hunger Games (85% certified fresh). Ever since the Mockingjays (both at 70%), critics’ love for Hunger Games has waned with Songbirds and Snakes being the worst reviewed in franchise at 64%.

The Hunger Games franchise through its five previous movies has minted $3.3 billion at the global box office.

#3274. I’m a Deals Writer, and These Are My Top 10 Tech Deals This Week

As Lifehacker's deals writer, I'm always looking for the best bargains on TVs, speakers, laptops, and other tech. Now that it's Friday, I've rounded up this week's sales highlights.

This week, you can already feel the early Black Friday deals heating up with the sale starting next week. Amazon has many tech deals, as do Costco, Walmart, and other retailers. You can find price cuts on the M5 MacBook Air, the best headphones of 2026, Kindle readers, and more.

The Sony WH-1000XM6 are one of the best premium headphones of 2026, and right now, Amazon is offering them with a 24% on them right now. That brings the price of the Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones down to $348. You're not likely to see these headphones drop any further in price anytime soon, even with Black Friday coming up. So if you've had your eyes on the XM6, this is likely the best deal you'll get for a while.

The Kindle Paperwhite is having one of its best discounts right now, dropping to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors. This is the classic, standard e-reader from Amazon, but since it's not the Signature Edition, you'll have to put up with ads and the minimum 16GB storage (which still gets you storage for over a thousand e-books). There are other e-readers on sale as well if you want to see other options.

The MacBook Air with the M5 chip comes in both 13-inch and 15-inch sizes, and if you're interested in either, it's a good time to buy: Amazon is selling both right now at a $250 discount. That brings the 13-inch MacBook Air to $1,049.99 (down from $1,299) and the 15-inch MacBook Air to $1,249 (originally $1,499), reaching their lowest prices since the June price hikes.

Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones are down to $199 from $359, saving you $160 and bringing them to their lowest price yet. Weighing around 8.1 ounces, they’re among the lightest premium noise-canceling headphones, with generously padded earcups and a cushioned headband that spreads pressure without gripping too tightly. They’re also easy to pack for travel, as the earcups fold and swivel for storage in the included hard-shell carrying case.

The Bose SoundLink Plus hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers,” and it’s down to $179 (originally $269). This is a great opportunity to snatch a quality portable speaker with a big discount.

Amazon has cut the price of its latest Fire TV Stick 4K, dropping it to $19.99 from $59.99 and bringing it to its lowest price ever. At this price, it's an affordable way to bring 4K streaming to an older television or give a sluggish smart TV a performance upgrade.

The Sony WH-CH730N are $98 (originally $179), the lowest price they've ever been. They use the same Sony Connect app as the premium headphones; as a result, you get a 10-band slider on the EQ menu, a battery care feature that extends the longevity of your battery life, 50 hours of juice, ANC, Ambient Sound (transparency mode), Multipoint to connect to two devices at once, and Bluetooth 6.0.

Samsung’s HW-Q600F soundbar is down to $379.99 at Amazon from $499.99, a $120 discount that brings it to its lowest price ever. This 2025 model sits in the middle of Samsung’s Q-Series lineup and pairs a sleek, angular bar with a subwoofer in a 3.1.2 setup. Dolby Atmos also brings a modest sense of height, and effects track cleanly from left to right. You get a graphic equalizer and sound presets for adjusting the audio to your preferences through the included remote.

The Ultimate Ears Miniroll is down to $49.99 (originally $79.99), the second-lowest it has sold for so far. It’s a small, flat, puck-shaped Bluetooth speaker that weighs just over half a pound, with a removable rubber strap you can attach to a backpack, bike handlebar, or shower caddy. Despite its size, the Miniroll can get surprisingly loud—which PCMag confirms in its review—and at moderate volume, it has enough sound for a kitchen or backyard without sounding thin. As for its battery life, you get about 12 hours of playback before it needs a charge over USB-C, while its IP67 rating protects it from dust and a brief dunk in water.

If you're looking for a premium model, Samsung’s 65-inch S90H OLED TV is down to $1,397.99 from $2,697.99 at launch, saving you over $1,000. The sale price is easier to justify when you consider that this is a new 2026 model. If the 65-inch model does not suit your space, Samsung also sells the S90H in 42-, 48-, 55-, 77-, and 83-inch versions, and those sizes are discounted as well.

#3271. Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, said last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

#3269. Next year’s iPhone Pro redesign sounds like exactly what I’ve been wanting

Rumors about next year’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models have been ramping up, and they suggest Apple is designing an ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ that combines traits from two current models.

Apple keeps expanding the iPhone line to include new models. And while it’s great that there are more models for differing preferences and needs, it’s also left me missing the days of having one model that was the clear “best.”

That problem isn’t going away, since the iPhone Duo represents a brand new type of iPhone that some users will love, while others find it isn’t for them.

With my failed iPhone Duo experiment over, I’m back to using iPhone 18 Pro as my default model. But I still have an iPhone Air around for work, and every time I pick it up, I’m struck by how impressive it remains.

I used the iPhone Air all of last year and loved it. The main reason I upgraded to an iPhone 18 Pro is the camera system. I have young children at home—including newborn twins—and want to capture the best possible photos before they get older.

iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera has been fantastic, and it’s great having the Telephoto again too.

But I still sorely miss the overall design of the iPhone Air. And it sounds like next year, I could get the best of both models.

Rumors indicate Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone Pro models will have a unique new design featuring a quad-curved display that makes it look bezel-free.

The new models are expected to also be a bit slimmer, use curved edges, and possibly even bring back titanium. Leakers say the new design borrows a lot from the iPhone Air’s look.

This sounds like exactly what I’ve been hoping for.

While the ‘iPhone 20 Pro’ certainly won’t—and shouldn’t—be as thin as iPhone Air, if it can slim down a little and adopt several other Air design traits, I suspect it will evoke the same affection the Air has.

But unlike the Air, the new Pro model will still offer the best camera system in an iPhone (not to mention better battery life).

As a huge fan of the design of the Air, and the functionality of the 18 Pro, Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone model could prove the perfect model for me. And for anyone else not opting for iPhone Duo 2.

What do you think of the rumored iPhone 20 Pro design? Let us know in the comments.

#3268. I tested the Xreal Aura glasses for 2 weeks — amazing displays and immersive spatial computing let down by a lack of apps

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Xreal and Google's first foray into XR glasses is a fascinating look at the future of AR and VR devices. But that also means you're prototyping something that will get better, but maybe not yet.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

For quite awhile I have firmly believed that smart glasses are the next device that will evolve the future of computing, much like the iPhone heralded the next 20 years of tech progression. And this is despite the current "pervert glasses" backlash.

I am fascinated by the sudden influx of AR and XR glasses that offer immersive environments and while also looking "normal." I've already tried Meta VR Glasses and Snap Specs, but neither are actually available for everyone yet. The Google, Qualcomm and Xreal collaboration Aura glasses are.

All three glasses could be considered VR-lite, but I think they're about finding a use between AI glasses and wearing a full headset.

In that way, the Auras are the escaped experiment worth investigating. Following the Samsung Galaxy XR headset, these are just the second device to run Google's Android XR platform natively.

This first stab at an XR headset that I think most people will want is impressive and a great example of what Android XR could be, but it also means you're the guinea pig with all that implies.

Xreal S1 andQualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform

Right when the Aura launched on November 17, I put together some early impressions of the glassese. For the most part, my thoughts haven't changed. But after using the glasses more, some plusses and minuses have solidified.

I am not an advocate for VR as it currently works with bulky, isolating headsets. However, I can still be impressed virtual reality experiences.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Xreal Aura provides that with 6DoF spatial computing. The two temple cameras and the nose bridge camera enable pinch gesture controls and you can always use the puck as trackpad, which I defaulted to more often that not.

The pinch controls work well. Occasionally the hitbox was a hair off but I didn't notice lag when I adjusted. I will note that in darker environments, it didn't always work, which isn't totally surprising but something to know.

Out of the box, the Auras come with a variety of mixed-reality experiences, from a VR tour of the Galapagos, to some games and a 360 version of Google Maps that is a delight to explore.

VR enthusiasts will find the 70-degree field of view limiting but I wasn't bothered by it. Watching movies feels like you're in a theater for yourself, and extending my desktop workspace was seamless via the wired accessory cable (or wireless for some devices).

These might be the best displays Xreal has made to date. I tested the refreshed Xreal One Pro Plus a couple of weeks ago and thought it was an improvement, and now the Aura is taking it even further.

Xreal lists the resolution of the Aura's as 1,920 x 1,200 per eye (1200p). It makes for sharp images, especially in games and media. It feels premium.

The color gamut isn't robust and the Aura doesn't offer HDR like the One Pro Plus, but if you don't need that level of display detail, these look good. Plus, with 1200 nits of brightness, the display can handle a number of settings. And the electrochromic dimming gets pretty dark, meaning you should feel more immersed.

Personally, I have never had great luck reading text as is on AR glasses, and while the Aura's are better, you may find text blurry. Fortunately, you can zoom in, which helps.

One advantage the Xreal Aura glasses have over Meta's VR Glasses and the Snap Specs is the built-in Google ecosystem. Snap and Meta have both promised that they're building up their developer connections to create more apps for their glasses, but Google's slew of in-house designs and third-party apps is already robust.

On the productivity side, you've got the entire Google suite from Docs and Drive to your calendar and Gmail. Plus, there's the Google Play Store with normal phone games and a small but growing number of XR-specific apps.

Moving forward, as Android XR grows, this will be what sets the Aura and future Android XR devices apart from Snap and Meta.

Here's the rub: you don't really need XR glasses yet. Xreal's own lineup of AR glasses are already great for productivity, gaming and watching content by connecting to your laptop, mini PC, phone or gaming device.

Because of that, the flaws do stand out a bit more.

If we're thinking of the Aura as VR-lite, especially compared to the Meta VR Glasses, then the biggest missing component for the Xreal Aura glasses is games.

Yes, I did try Demeo, which was fun, and HoloChess, which felt like the Star Wars version of chess. But from what I could tell, there aren't many native XR/VR games on the Play Store, while the Meta Quest Store has hundreds, and Meta promised at least 75 launch titles specifically designed for the VR glasses next year.

You can play 2D games on the Play Store, which I did with some games I already have on my account. Xreal is selling its own first-party controller made with GameSir, but you can use any Bluetooth controller. Again, you can connect other Xreal glasses to your phone, laptop, or gaming device with a controller as well.

It's not clear how long it'll take native Android XR experiences to catch up to Meta, but for now, Meta has the lead.

Xreal rates the battery life of the Aura puck between three and four hours. I found that to be pretty accurate. In my testing watching an hour-long YouTube video and then playing some games for about 20 minutes knocked the battery life from 100% to about 80%.

I debated putting this as a flaw because I'm not sure if you want to keep these glasses on for more than three hours. Perhaps that is the sweet spot. Still, for anything longer, you'll need to recharge.

That said, heat becomes a concern. The puck can get warm, but it does include a fan to dissipate heat. Surprisingly, the glasses can get quite warm, especially in the area that runs across your forehead.

General use seemed okay, but at one point I accidentally turned on screen recording and I could feel the glasses heating up. It never got laptop-panini levels of hot, but as the tech ages, I foresee this being a problem.

The Xreal Auras have just three cameras. Two on the temples and one on the nose bridge. As mentioned, I find the hand tracking pretty decent and pinch gestures work well.

However, I've also worn the Meta VR Glasses, which have 6 external cameras and four internal ones. Fundamentally, Xreal adding seven more cameras would change the design of the glasses, which you can see in the ski-goggle look of Meta's forthcoming platform.

Still, eye tracking makes navigating the XR space better. And compared to Meta, where you can leave your hand on the table or in your lap and still use gesture controls, the three-camera Aura setup is more limiting.

The pushback is the puck trackpad, which I used most frequently. I am comfortable with trackpads and mice, and the puck is a nice midway point.

The puck is a mini-PC with glasses attached, but that doesn't make navigation the best without accessories or the trackpad.

If Xreal's next iteration can add eye tracking or even a couple more external cameras, the already good hand tracking would be even better.

I find the Xreal Aura glasses fascinating, and when its rivals finally launch, I think a new space in the tech world will open up that is more than just pervert glasses and bulky headsets. Perhaps I've given these glasses more grace than future versions will deserve, but for a first go in this space, I'm excited by the potential.

For many, I'm not sure the $1,000+ price tag is cheap enough to dive in, but for the curious and the early adopters, this is a device of potential. It hints at what mixed reality wearables could be.

When I use the Aura, I get what it's supposed to be. It's the taste of a Vision Pro or Quest headset in a lighter, more comfortable package. Xreal has set the bar; it'll be up to everyone to see if they can raise it.

#3266. ‘Percy Jackson’: How A Quest To Save Annabeth Makes Everyone Reevaluate Their Relationships In Season 3

SPOILER ALERT! This post contains some details from the first two episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3.

If there is one thing that the kids of Camp Half-Blood can count on, it’s that their lives are only going to get more complicated.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians returned to Disney+ for Season 3 on Friday, and already the dynamics have shifted. The first episode opens with Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries) recruiting the recently revived child of Zeus, Thalia (Tamara Smart), to help them rescue two younger demigods — Nico and Bianca di Angelo, the children of Hades — and the tension is palpable. Related Stories Casting 'Afterlife With Archie' Disney+ Series Casts Its Archie, Veronica, Betty, Jughead & Sabrina News 'Gilmore Girls: A Year In The Life' Gets New Home On Hulu After Netflix Deal Ends, Release Date Set

“I think that Annabeth’s presence is actually incredibly divisive between the two of them,” Smart tells Deadline of the dynamic between Thalia and Percy. Watch on Deadline

In terms of sowing that division on screen, she adds that “a lot of it is based in our actual relationship in the best of ways.”

“Walker also has the exact same personality and sense of humor. So, right right off the bat, we were definitely going back and forth and joking, and I think the only thing we had to do was just up the stakes and be serious about it, which was actually more difficult than we planned,” she says.

Percy and Thalia can’t agree on almost anything, except their loyalty to Annabeth, who has unwittingly been thrown in the middle of their power struggle at the start of the season.

So, when Annabeth is captured and brought to an enemy stronghold where she’s forced to bear the weight of the sky (the eponymous Titan’s Curse), those two have to set aside their differences quite quickly.

“She kind of kept them at a safe distance away from each other, because, as I guess we’ve seen the trailer, bad things happen when they’re not at that safe distance,” Scobell says. “So I think without her there, they’re forced to actually work together and try to figure each other out and attempt to understand each other.”

Adds Smart: “They actually have to be forced into proximity to work together to get her back, because that’s their mutual interest. So, it’s really beautiful in a way that her absence brings them closer, which is a very human thing for us. I think as people, we’re just always brought closer by tragedy. But I think that for them specifically, a lot of ego has to get out the door for them to work together to achieve their mutual goal.”

Rather than put a wedge in Annabeth’s relationship with either, Jeffries thinks that the tension between Percy and Thalia also provides some clarity for the daughter of Athena. Whether she’s ready to face that realization yet is another story.

“I honestly feel like you get to see more Percabeth when it’s between Percy and Thalia,” Jeffries says. “I feel like her eyes open up a little bit. Annabeth is very smart. Even though she’s making it look like she’s not noticing, she knows [she’s developing feelings for Percy]. I don’t know if that’s more of like a denial between her of like, ‘No, no, I’m working right now. I’m on missions. I don’t have time to be falling in love…’

She continues: “You get to see the fight [in her] more, not physically, but just like ‘No, I love this person. You’re not gonna take him away from me.'”

United States Capitol, First Street Southeast, Washington, DC, USA

Cursor plans to explore dropping Chinese open-weight AI models because of “geopolitical risk”, a House investigation says. The SpaceX-owned coding platform built its flagship model, Composer 2, on Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.5.

CNBC’s Kai Nicol-Schwarz first reported the plan from an advance copy of the report. The House Homeland Security Committee and the Select Committee on China released the joint report on Friday. It says Anysphere, Cursor’s developer, told them of its plans.

Anysphere “plans to explore phasing out PRC-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk,” the committees wrote.

The report describes an exploratory plan, with no decision or timetable. Cursor, SpaceX and DoorDash did not respond to CNBC’s request for comment, and Airbnb declined to comment.

The committees opened their inquiry in April with letters to Anysphere and Airbnb, and added DoorDash in July. All three use Chinese models in different ways, the report found.

Airbnb runs customised versions of Alibaba’s Qwen on US servers. One powers an assistant handling about 80,000 guest and host conversations a day. Another summarises about 250,000 support cases and calls daily.

DoorDash reported 25 Chinese model families in real use, meaning each cost at least $5,000 to run. Swapping out one model built into a larger system could take up to six months. Most other uses could switch almost at once, it said.

For Cursor, the committees said the Chinese base became public only after an outside developer identified it. Cursor’s own technical report names Kimi K2.5 as the starting point. Cursor then trained it further on code. SpaceX completed its purchase of Cursor in August, at an implied $60bn equity value, according to CNBC.

Cost, customisation and near-frontier performance drive adoption, the report found. The US lacks an open-weight rival at the right price. The report also says much of China’s progress rests on capabilities taken from American models. In September, OpenAI said Moonshot-linked users had tried to extract its AI reasoning. Hosting a model in the US keeps data out of China, the committees add. But it does not change how the model was trained.

The committees want to extend the federal DeepSeek ban to other Chinese developers. Their models would also be kept out of federal contract work and high-risk critical infrastructure. They also call for a model provenance standard and a national American open-weight initiative.

They warn against moving too fast. Forcing companies off Chinese models before trusted alternatives exist would raise costs, the report says. It would also hand the market to a few closed providers. It points to new open models from Reflection AI and Mistral as encouraging signs.

The same question is playing out in India. Sarvam, the startup backed by the government’s IndiaAI Mission to build a homegrown model, has begun selling access to DeepSeek and other Chinese models, Bloomberg’s Saritha Rai reported.

Its new Token Factory service hosts models from DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai in India, alongside Sarvam’s own model and Google’s Gemma. It already serves more than 450bn tokens a day on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Sarvam said. Critics online asked why a lab built on subsidised compute was reselling Chinese models.

“We haven’t changed our motto. We continue to build AI models for India,” co-founder Pratyush Kumar told Bloomberg.

Co-founder Vivek Raghavan said the chips behind the service are “entirely funded by private money”. Keeping inference in India also keeps users’ data in the country, he added.

Sarvam has defenders. Nikhil Pahwa, MediaNama’s founder, told the site that Sarvam has to earn money in an open market. The criticism came days after Sarvam signed a deal with India’s defence ministry to build AI tools for the armed forces, MediaNama reported. The startup became India’s newest AI unicorn in June.
